evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'this should take about ten to fifteen minutes so we can provide you an accurate estimate' but customer immediately pushes back saying 'we can share quickly rather than ten to 15 minutes' and rep acquiesces without really waiting for a yes or re-framing. No clear 'Does that sound good to you?' pause.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asks 'what are your biggest concerns for this upcoming move and what are the most important things you'd like answers to on this call today aside from the pricing?' but this comes AFTER he's already asked about move date, property type, and size in Section 1. This is asked after discovery probing has started, not before.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer says 'only a normal like a one or two so far small Sofer and 22 beds and one TV.' Rep responds 'Okay, so just the, okay, the big staff you're concerned about it.' Then rep immediately pivots to listing items: 'Well yeah so so far from what I have, so you have like two couches, is that correct?' This is item inventory, not two-layer follow-up on any expressed concern. No genuine 'tell me more about that' deepening.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection. Rep confirms details item-by-item ('Okay, two sofas') but never reflects back a consolidated picture of the customer's concerns or priorities.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covers: property type (apartment), floor (second), rooms (two bedroom), walking distance (40 feet), additional stops (Plano destination), special considerations (stairs, TV, bunk bed, disassembly needs). All major logistics items addressed.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep never asks 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' He discusses it only when customer volunteers they will pack themselves.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes. Rep says 'a typical two bedroom apartment usually has 25 to 35 boxes packed with belongings. So do you feel like you will fall within this range?' Customer responds '15 boxes'.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides range: 'it's safe to budget around $3,753 to $3,945' for 9–10 hours. Personalizes to 'second floor apartment to another second floor apartment with four hours drive in between.' Later adjusts to 8.5 hours = $3,657 or 7 hours = $3,369 based on customer's scenario.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep discloses trip fee ($2,025), explains hourly rate ($192/hr for two movers), lists what's included (fuel, taxes, insurance, pads, wraps, tools, disassembly/reassembly). Mentions 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments. No hidden fees stated multiple times. However, there is confusion around whether the $2,025 trip fee is charged separately or included, and rep's explanation of packing material charges creates back-and-forth friction.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked. Rep gives estimate and customer immediately asks clarifying questions about pricing structure. No 'Does that feel fair to you?' or similar pause for reflection.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep says 'Our on time guarantee. So, if we can't make it in the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill and all of that is included at no extra cost.' Covers discount framing clearly.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep says 'we'll provide up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages. Unlike our competitors, so either charge extra or offer only state mandated 60¢ per pound coverage' and 'it's included in the hourly rate, no additional cost.' Covers amount, no deductible framing, and built-in status.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar after delivering the Two Promises. No explicit loop-close.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep asks 'Will there be anything else?' which is a throwaway yes/no. Not a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No. Never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or similar catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep says 'So would you like to, would you like our help with your, with your move for Monday September 28th?' This is a plain ask. However, customer deflects with a timing question, and rep then pivots immediately into logistical details (8:30 AM start time, same-day delivery) and the customer says 'Yeah, please send the quote. I will respond to you.' The call ends without a clear yes-to-booking, so while the ask was made plainly, there was an implicit out: 'send me the quote and I'll get back to you.' This is borderline; the ask was direct but the follow-through allowed an easy escape.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Yes. Rep says 'we don't collect a front payment, no deposit as well' which signals rate is locked without deposit.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep confirms: arrival window (8:30 AM–9:00 AM, trying for 8:00 AM), date (Monday September 28th), pickup address (implied from earlier), delivery address (Plano, stated). But customer never fully commits to the booking—only asks to receive the quote via email. Phone number is never confirmed, and no crew notes about customer's concerns (boxes, TV, bunk bed) are explicitly noted for the crew.

top_strength: Excellent logistics detail-gathering and pricing transparency—rep captured all seven logistics items (property type, floor, rooms, walking distance, additional stops, special considerations, ancillary items) and delivered comprehensive fee disclosure with no-hidden-fees messaging repeated multiple times.
coaching_note: Skip 'Their Agenda' until after the initial discovery in Section 1 is complete, then follow any concern raised with genuine two-layer follow-up ("tell me more about that") and close Section 2 with a summary reflection—rep left money on the table by diving straight into item inventory rather than uncovering real pain points.
